final_rationale: The verdict remains noncompliant because the Actor provided no genuinely new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record. That reframing is partly valid: the available evidence supports aggregate readiness and supports documenting limitations and monitoring in general. But the controlling internal predicate is narrower and unresolved. Admissible evidence shows a 2.1-point gap in a segment named in three international pilot commitments, policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and legal review is still open. A caveated certification narrative is not equivalent to evidence that the required disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance actually exists. Because the caveat here points to an unmet compliance condition rather than merely a residual risk to be monitored, proportional treatment does not justify moving to compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the Spanish-language billing support gap was resolved before launch.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering this material limitation before launch.
No admissible evidence shows a released or launch-ready disclosure artifact satisfying the model-card requirement for the named launch use case.
The affected segment is named in three international pilot commitments, which meets the policy materiality trigger.
Legal review remains open, so product's non-core characterization does not resolve materiality on this record.
Aggregate launch readiness and clean rehearsal results do not satisfy the separate disclosure-or-risk-acceptance predicate required by policy.
